title: Gonadal PIP-seq reveals genes with enriched expression during germ cell development and sexual differentiation in sea lamprey (Petromyzon marinus Linnaeus).
abstract: The sea lamprey (Petromyzon marinus Linnaeus) is an extant jawless vertebrate that remains sexually labile in larval stage. Their gonad contains bipotential, female, and male germ cells before metamorphosis. To examine the genetic programs during germ cell development and differentiation, we profiled transcriptomes of dissociated gonadal cells from larvae and metamorphosed transformers (sex-determined) using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (BD FACS Aria IIu) and PIPseqTM (Fluent BioSciences/Illumina). The detected primordial germ cells exhibited genes enriched in cell fate commitment, cellular response to lipopolysaccharide, protein folding, and regulation of gene expression and RNA splicing. The female germ cells we assessed differentially expressed aep1, cuzd1, s100a1, and zp genes from multiple loci. Pseudotime trajectory and Gene Ontology analyses of genes changing along the female differentiation pathway revealed enrichment in genes involved in binding of sperm to zona pellucida, egg coat formation, prevention of polyspermy, and positive regulation of acrosome reaction. On the other hand, genes enriched in a male differentiation pathway were involved in cell cycle, DNA replication and repair, transcription and mRNA splicing and rRNA maturation, ribosome assembly and translation, and protein folding, modification and catabolism. Sea lamprey germ cell development likely requires numerous genes that regulate germ cell specification and differentiation.

title: Phase and Conformational Transitions in Biomolecules and Polymers With Nanopores.
abstract: Phase transitions have been studied extensively for a long time, both experimentally and theoretically, to understand physical, chemical, and biological processes. Here, we focus mainly on biological molecules for which changes in state or conformation are correlated with their biological function, pathological implications, or potential biotechnology applications. We discuss how a nanohole, or a nanopore, with electrical detection could detect and characterize the phase transition of biological macromolecules in confined media. We illustrate the review with emblematic molecules of life: nucleic acids and proteins. We discuss DNA and RNA denaturation, their compaction and decompaction; we also discuss protein folding using different approaches, denaturing agents, electric forces, molecular motors, and their aggregation. Finally, we present polymer phase transitions or conformational modifications to characterize polymer size or detect biomarkers. The studies presented here are discussed in comparison with other single-molecule approaches. We also discuss the potential contributions of nanopore approaches to resolving biological questions or to applications.

title: Elevated ATP-Citrate Lyase Links Hyperglycemic Metabolism to Maternal Diabetes-Induced Neural Tube Defects.
abstract: The pathogenesis of neural tube defects (NTDs) precipitated by maternal diabetes mellitus (DM) encompasses a cascade of intricate cellular processes, prominently featuring excessive apoptosis. The critical metabolic mediators bridging hyperglycemic metabolism to apoptotic pathways remain unidentified, particularly in human contexts. Elevated expression of ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY), a metabolic enzyme catalyzing the synthesis of acetyl-CoA from glucose, was discerned in cranial neural tube exposed to maternal diabetes. Inhibition of ACLY effectively normalized hyperglycemia-induced augmented levels of acetyl-CoA and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac). ACLY inhibitor hydroxycitric acid (HCA) mitigated the elevated acetyl-CoA and H3K27ac levels and reduced the incidence of NTDs caused by maternal diabetes. Integrated analyses of H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation (CHIP)-seq and RNA-seq data unveiled a correlation between aberrant H3K27ac occupancy and genome-wide gene dysregulation. The most upregulated gene, thioredoxin-interacting protein (Txnip) coupled with downstream phosphorylation of ASK1 and heightened apoptosis, was prominently observed in cranial neural tube with maternal diabetes, which can be attenuated by inhibition of ACLY. Corroborative evidence from human subjects with diabetes-associated NTDs substantiated this pathogenicity. Our findings underscore the pivotal role of ACLY in linking hyperglycemic metabolism to NTDs, highlighting the potential prophylactic utility of HCA supplementation in preventing maternal diabetes-induced public health issues.

title: Identification of key pathways and functional modules associated with multiple abiotic and biotic stress conditions in barley.
abstract: Barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) is frequently exposed to diverse abiotic and biotic stresses that threaten its productivity and quality. This study aimed to identify key pathways, gene modules, and hub genes associated with multiple stress conditions in barley using a weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). A total of 515 RNA-Seq samples representing 14 different stress types were integrated and analyzed to construct a comprehensive co-expression network. Eleven distinct gene modules were identified, five of which showed significant correlations with abiotic and/or biotic stresses. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses revealed that these modules are primarily involved in energy metabolism, amino acid biosynthesis, carbon metabolism, and protein processing-pathways critical for stress adaptation. The black and pink modules were associated with metabolic regulation and structural stability under abiotic stress, whereas the blue and green modules were linked to protein turnover and pathogen response during biotic stress. The red module highlighted the downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation under both stress types, indicating energy conservation mechanisms. Collectively, these findings provide novel insights into the coordinated transcriptional networks that regulate stress resilience in barley and identify potential molecular targets for breeding and biotechnological improvement of multi-stress tolerance.

title: GLUD1 mediates leucine signaling to restrain POLRMT proteolysis and promote mitochondrial biogenesis.
abstract: Mitochondria maintain unique biogenesis programs (mitobiogenesis) to encode key components in oxidative phosphorylation system in response to metabolic cues. How mitochondria integrate specific metabolite signals into mitobiogenesis remains elusive. Here, we report that pancreatic cancer cells employ glutamate dehydrogenase 1 (GLUD1) to couple leucine signaling and mitobiogenesis. Mitochondrial RNA polymerase (POLRMT) positively correlates with GLUD1 at proteomic level, but not transcriptomic level, in cancer cell lines. GLUD1 maintains POLRMT protein, mitochondrial genome (mtDNA)-encoded protein expression, and mitochondrial mass independent of its catalytic activity. Notably, GLUD1 interacts with POLRMT and protects it from caspase 9 (CASP9)-mediated proteolysis. Metabolite screening reveals that leucine, an abundant amino acid in mtDNA-encoded proteins, enhances GLUD1 binding to stabilize POLRMT. Depletion of solute carrier family 25 member 44 (SLC25A44), the mitochondrial leucine transporter, reduces POLRMT protein and suppresses mitobiogenesis. GLUD1-mediated leucine signaling supports mitochondrial respiration and pancreatic cancer cell growth in culture and in vivo. Clinical pancreatic tumor tissues accumulate leucine and upregulate GLUD1, which is linked to enhanced mitobiogenesis. Together, GLUD1 mediates leucine signaling to support mitobiogenesis and pancreatic cancer development.

title: Plasma proteins associated with maladaptive kidney cell states and kidney function: a single-cell-informed Mendelian randomisation study.
abstract: To assess genetic associations with kidney function for plasma proteins linked to maladaptive kidney cell states. We combined donor-paired single-nucleus RNA sequencing (304,989 nuclei from 80 donors) with plasma cis-protein quantitative trait loci to define candidates across four cell states. Cis-Mendelian randomisation (MR) tested creatinine-based estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in approximately 1.2 million participants. Follow-up used CKDGen and FinnGen kidney outcomes. We performed single-signal colocalisation and a multi-signal sensitivity analysis for six prioritised candidates. Of 259 candidates, 228 yielded an eGFR MR estimate and 17 met the discovery false discovery rate threshold. We found no evidence of enrichment of significant MR associations amongst candidates (odds ratio 0.66, 95% confidence interval 0.37-1.11). In the matched Olink analysis, 80.8% of candidates and 69.7% of other proteins were higher at lower eGFR (odds ratio 1.82, P = 0.0038). Six candidates met the original prioritisation criteria. Only TFPI showed directionally concordant nominal associations in FinnGen, for renal failure and diabetic nephropathy. SORT1 had the strongest shared-variant evidence with eGFR (single-signal posterior probability 0.924 at the primary prior). Single-nucleus expression and cis-MR identified a subset of candidates for follow-up, with differing support across loci and kidney outcomes. Tissue expression contextualises the plasma associations. Cellular origin and the effects of therapeutic modulation require direct evaluation.

title: Atractylodin remodels microglial lipid metabolism through deoxycholic acid signaling to suppress neuronal ferroptosis and alleviate depression-like behaviors.
abstract: Chronic stress can disrupt hippocampal neuroimmune and metabolic homeostasis, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Atractylodin is a naturally occurring bioactive compound with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and metabolic regulatory activities. Its potential to ameliorate chronic stress-associated neuroimmune and metabolic disturbances warrants investigation, but its mechanisms of action remain unclear. To determine whether atractylodin (ATR) alleviates chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced depression-like behaviors by restoring deoxycholic acid (DCA) signaling and microglial lipid homeostasis. A multilevel study integrated CUMS mice, hippocampal multi-omics, public human major depressive disorder single-nucleus RNA sequencing, microglia-neuron conditioned-medium experiments, and in vivo rescue and blockade interventions. Behavioral, histological, and molecular analyses evaluated ATR efficacy. DCA was prioritized through untargeted metabolomics and targeted bile acid profiling. Mechanistic studies combined BV2 transcriptomics and lipidomics with inhibition of G protein-coupled bile acid receptor 1 (TGR5/GPBAR1), stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1 (SCD1) knockdown, oleic acid rescue, and conditioned-medium transfer to HT22 cells. Antibiotic treatment, DCA supplementation, and TGR5 inhibition were used for in vivo validation. ATR improved depression-like behaviors and hippocampal injury while restoring serum and hippocampal DCA. DCA remodeled the BV2 lipidome through TGR5-SCD1 signaling, restored unsaturated lipid signatures, and reduced lipid accumulation and pathological activation. TGR5 inhibition or SCD1 knockdown weakened these effects, whereas oleic acid partially rescued the SCD1-deficient phenotype. Conditioned medium from DCA-treated BV2 cells attenuated lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial injury, and ferroptosis-associated changes in HT22 cells. In vivo, antibiotics weakened ATR-mediated protection, DCA supplementation partially restored it, and TGR5 inhibition attenuated this protection. ATR restores DCA-dependent TGR5-SCD1 signaling to remodel microglial lipid metabolism, thereby suppressing microglia-mediated neuronal ferroptosis and alleviating depression-like behaviors.

title: Integrative network toxicology, transcriptomic analysis, and experimental validation identify TOP2A-associated molecular alterations in NNK-related hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Accumulating evidence implicates nicotine-derived nitrosamine ketone (NNK) in the pathogenesis of various malignancies, yet the biological pathways underlying its effects on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) have not been fully elucidated. To characterize the signaling pathways involved in NNK-driven hepatocellular carcinoma, we jointly applied network toxicology, single-cell RNA sequencing, molecular docking, virtual knockout analysis, and in vitro validation. Database mining identified 502 putative NNK-related targets across ChEMBL, CTD, SEA, and SwissTarget, together with 2143 HCC-associated genes retrieved from GeneCards, OMIM, and TTD. Functional enrichment analyses implicated the candidate genes in xenobiotic responses, cell cycle regulation, transcription factor binding, and several cancer-related signaling pathways, particularly the PI3K-Akt, FoxO, and p53 pathways. Following transcriptomic validation in GSE121248 and machine learning prioritization, TOP2A emerged as the leading candidate associated with NNK-related molecular alterations in HCC. TOP2A showed satisfactory discriminatory performance in both GSE121248 and GSE14520, with AUC values exceeding 0.75. Immune cell deconvolution further revealed associations between TOP2A expression and multiple immune cell subsets. In silico gene perturbation analysis identified ORM1 as a candidate gene associated with predicted TOP2A perturbation, suggesting a potential molecular relationship between TOP2A and ORM1 rather than an experimentally established regulatory axis. Subsequent cellular experiments showed that NNK treatment increased growth-related cellular activity and migratory phenotypes in both HuH-7 and Hep 3B2.1-7 cells. NNK exposure was also accompanied by increased TOP2A and ORM1 protein abundance, with consistent western blot findings observed in both HCC cell lines. In summary, this study identifies TOP2A as a potential molecular candidate associated with NNK-related HCC progression and suggests a possible relationship between TOP2A and ORM1 that may contribute to NNK-associated molecular alterations in HCC.

title: Clostridioides difficile colitis promotes neuroinflammatory responses in the prefrontal cortex: a preclinical study in mice.
abstract: Recurrent and severe Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a significant problem in the elderly. There is growing evidence that intestinal dysbiosis and inflammation, characteristic features of CDI, can influence brain function. We examined whether neuroinflammatory responses occur during CDI and employed a spatial metabolomic and transcriptomic approach, integrated with biomolecular analyses, to characterize these responses in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) of a CDI mouse model. 6-month-old mice were infected with C. difficile and euthanized on days 3, 4, and 7 post-infection (p.i.) for spatial metabolic analysis, bulk RNA-sequencing of the PFC, or systemic and gut inflammation analysis. Infected mice developed diarrhea and weight loss that peaked by day 3 and resolved by day 7. Spatial metabolomics analysis of the infected brain tissues indicated an imbalance of various neuroprotective metabolites in the PFC on day 4. Differential gene expression analysis identified 124 differentially expressed genes on day 7. Gene set enrichment analysis identified upregulation of pathways associated with neurodegenerative diseases and oxidative phosphorylation in infected mice. PFC protein and transcripts levels of GFAP (glial fibrillary acidic protein) were increased in infected mice, indicating a reactive astrocyte response. Increased levels of lipocalin-2 (Lcn2), myeloperoxidase (MPO), calprotectin (S100A8/A9), IL-33, and IL-13 were also found in the PFC of infected mice. Levels of fecal Lcn2, a marker of intestinal epithelial barrier disruption, correlate positively with the levels of Lcn2, MPO, and S100A8/A9 in the PFC. Our findings show that CDI, in a mouse model, induces metabolomic and transcriptomic changes in the PFC, including genes associated with oxidative phosphorylation and neurodegeneration.

title: Genome‑wide analysis of the maize CK1 family and functional characterization of ZmCK1-8 in modulating root architecture and nitrate‑responsive physiological traits under low‑nitrogen conditions.
abstract: Nitrogen deficiency is a major constraint of global maize production. Although CK1 family members have diverse regulatory functions in eukaryotes, the CK1 family in maize has not yet been systematically identified, and their roles in maize nitrogen metabolism remain poorly understood. In the current study, we sought to identify the ZmCK1 family members and investigate the physiological and molecular roles of ZmCK1s in maize growth under low-nitrogen conditions. We identified 20 maize ZmCK1 family members and characterized them through phylogenetic analysis, motif and domain prediction, gene structure analysis, promoter cis-element annotation, and nitrate-responsive transcriptome profiling. ZmCK1-8, a nitrate-responsive gene, was selected for functional analysis. B73 and ZmCK1-8 mutants were hydroponically cultured under low-nitrogen conditions to assess root architecture, glutamine synthetase (GS), glutamate synthase (GOGAT), nitrate reductase (NR), and protein and nitrogen contents. The mutants exhibited enhanced root growth, suggesting that ZmCK1-8 plays a role in regulating root growth under low‑nitrogen condition and is associated with altered nitrogen‑related physiological traits. Transcriptomic analysis identified 256 and 660 genotype‑dependent nitrate‑responsive genes in ck1‑8‑1 and ck1‑8‑2 mutants, respectively, enriched in hormone signaling, stimulus responses, and transmembrane transporter activity. Loss of ZmCK1-8 was associated with upregulation of ZmGS1-5, and altered nitrogen-related physiological traits. Yeast two-hybrid and BiFC assays confirmed that ZmCK1-8 physically interacts with the chromatin remodeler ZmCHB101. RT-qPCR analysis of ZmCHB101 RNAi line further suggested that ZmCK1-8 and ZmCHB101 share several downstream targets, including ZmGS1-5, GOGAT, and ZmPTR11. In contrast, other nitrate-responsive genes, such as ZmPTR12, ZmNPF25, and ZmNPF34, showed distinct expression patterns between the two genetic backgrounds. Genome-wide analysis identified 20 ZmCK1 members, of which ZmCK1-8 was found to be associated with nitrate‑induced root growth. Loss of ZmCK1-8 function is associated with altered nitrogen-related physiological traits in roots, while ZmGS1-5 is identified as a candidate downstream responder. Furthermore, ZmCK1-8 physically interacts with ZmCHB101, though the mechanistic link between this interaction and target-gene regulation remains to be established. These results uncover a novel component of the maize nitrogen-signaling network and provide a candidate gene for further functional studies on low‑nitrogen adaptation in maize.

title: Multi-Omics- and Single-Cell-Guided Identification of GSK3B as an Actionable Target of Tilianin for Colorectal Cancer Therapy.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and therapeutic resistance and recurrence continue to limit clinical efficacy. Tilianin is a naturally derived flavonoid with reported antitumor activity, yet its therapeutic relevance and molecular mechanisms in CRC remain unclear. Here, we applied an integrated approach combining network pharmacology, machine learning, multi-omics analyses, single-cell RNA sequencing, molecular simulations, and experimental validation to elucidate the antitumor effects of tilianin in CRC. Ninety-seven overlapping targets between tilianin and CRC were identified, from which six key therapeutic genes (MMP3, MMP7, GSK3B, EPHB4, FAP, and CASP7) were prioritized using machine-learning algorithms. Immune infiltration and single-cell transcriptomic analyses suggested, at the computational-prediction level, that the tilianin-associated hub-gene network may be related to CRC tumor microenvironment features, particularly macrophage-, monocyte-, and epithelial cancer cell-associated signatures. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable and high-affinity interactions between tilianin and core target proteins. Functional assays confirmed that tilianin significantly inhibited CRC cell proliferation and migration, induced apoptosis, and downregulated the expression of the critical therapeutic target GSK3B. Collectively, these findings identify tilianin as a potential molecularly targeted therapeutic agent for CRC and provide experimentally supported evidence for its direct antitumor effects on CRC cells, while its immune-microenvironment-related effects remain computational hypotheses requiring further experimental validation.

title: Multi-omics profiling of primary human B cells activated via distinct stimuli.
abstract: B cells are central for immunity and immune-mediated diseases (IMD), but how distinct signaling pathways drive diverse activation responses over time is not comprehensively understood. Here, we obtain peripheral blood B cells from 27 female healthy donors for in vitro stimulation, profiling the response at multiple time points using RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq with surface protein markers (CITE-seq), and ATAC-seq. Using diverse stimuli including activation of the B cell receptor (BCR), Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7), TLR9, CD40, and differentiation into double negative 2 (DN2) IgD-CD27-CD11c+CD21- B cells, our analyses uncover activation-dependent B cell states, stimulation-specific transcription factors and regulatory regions, the dynamic response of IMD-associated gene expression, and specific open chromatin regions associated with IMD genetic risk. Furthermore, we also identify a lupus risk variant in an enhancer regulating TNFSF4 expression. The analysis data can be accessed via an interactive browser: https://mgalab.shinyapps.io/bcellactivation . Our findings underscore how profiling the full breadth of B cell activation pathways may be important for understanding B cell biology in health and disease.

title: Loureirin D alleviates ischemia-induced blood-brain barrier disruption via CD38-mediated suppression of microglial MAPK/JNK/ERK signaling.
abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a critical gatekeeper of central nervous system homeostasis, and its disruption represents a pivotal pathological mechanism underlying secondary brain injury and adverse clinical outcomes following ischemic stroke (IS). Consequently, therapeutic strategies aimed at preserving BBB integrity after ischemia hold substantial promise for IS treatment. Loureirin D, a bioactive flavonoid isolated from Dragon's blood, has demonstrated preliminary neuroprotective efficacy in photothrombotic stroke. However, whether BBB integrity is preserved in clinically relevant models of sustained, severe cerebral ischemia remains unknown, and the underlying molecular mechanisms remains to be elucidated. This study aimed to investigate whether Loureirin D protects against ischemia‑induced BBB disruption, and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms. Combined in vivo and in vitro mechanistic studies using rat permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pMCAO) model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD)‑exposed microglia‑endothelial co‑culture system. A rat model of pMCAO was established by intraluminal filament insertion. Neurological deficits and BBB integrity were evaluated by Bederson scoring, Evans blue extravasation, brain water content, IgG leakage, and western blot of tight junction (TJ) proteins (zonula occludens-1[ZO‑1], occludin) and matrix metalloproteinase 2/9 (MMP2/9). An OGD model and microglia‑endothelial co‑culture were used to recapitulate the ischemic neuroinflammatory microenvironment, and the endothelial barrier function was assessed using transendothelial electrical resistance and dextran permeability. Transcriptomic profiling, molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and small interfering RNA mediated knockdown were integrated to identify critical targets and mechanisms, with validation by western blot and immunofluorescence. Loureirin D markedly ameliorated neurological deficits and attenuated BBB disruption-as evidenced by reduced Evans blue extravasation, brain edema, and IgG leakage-and suppressed the ischemia‑induced upregulation of MMP2/9 in pMCAO rats. Furthermore, it restored the expression levels of ZO‑1 and occludin. In OGD‑exposed bEnd.3 cells, Loureirin D directly attenuated apoptosis, downregulated Bax and Caspase‑3 proteins, and suppressed reactive oxygen species generation. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis identified CD38 and Mapk11 as differentially expressed genes, and their dysregulation was subsequently validated at the mRNA level in ischemic brain tissues. Molecular docking simulations and CETSA, further supported by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay, collectively provided robust evidence for the direct physical interaction between Loureirin D and CD38. In OGD‑exposed BV2 microglial cells, Loureirin D suppressed microglial activation, as evidenced by reduced CD86 expression, and inhibited the phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPK), c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK), extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), and p38, thereby attenuating MMP2/9 secretion. In a microglia-endothelial cell co‑culture system, Loureirin D preserved endothelial TJ integrity, as demonstrated by the sustained expression and proper localization of ZO-1 and occludin. These protective effects were abolished by CD38 knockdown, indicating a CD38-dependent mechanism. Loureirin D inhibits microglia activation by specifically targeting CD38, thereby suppressing the MAPK-MMP-2/9 signaling cascade and preserving BBB integrity. Concurrently, it directly protects brain microvascular endothelial cells against apoptosis and oxidative stress. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic rationale for the therapeutic potential of Loureirin D in IS and provide a translational foundation for the development of CD38-targeted interventions for neurovascular protection in cerebrovascular diseases.

title: Network toxicology and single-cell transcriptomics identify acrylamide- and glycidamide-related candidate biomarkers in diabetic ulcers.
abstract: Diabetic ulcers (DU) are severe complications of diabetes, and environmental contaminants such as acrylamide (AA) and its metabolite glycidamide (GA) have been associated with metabolic disturbances relevant to diabetes. In this study, public transcriptomic datasets, network toxicology, protein interaction analysis, and machine learning were integrated to identify plausible candidate DU-associated biomarkers overlapping with predicted AA or GA targets. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and single-cell RNA sequencing were further applied to characterize their biological roles and cellular distribution. Eight candidate genes were identified from the intersection of differentially expressed genes and predicted toxicant targets, and PNP and CTSB were ultimately identified as plausible candidate DU-associated biomarkers. These genes were associated with proteasome function, DNA damage and repair, immune dysregulation, and altered cell communication. Single-cell analysis highlighted macrophages and T cells as major cell populations with dynamic plausible candidate biomarker expression. ELISA in streptozotocin induced diabetic ulcer mice further confirmed significantly increased CTSB and PNP protein levels, providing preliminary protein-level support for their association with DU. However, the overlap of PNP and CTSB with predicted AA/GA targets represents hypothesis-generating computational evidence only and does not establish that AA/GA exposure modulates these genes in vivo. These findings support PNP and CTSB as plausible candidate DU-associated biomarkers, while the predicted AA/GA-related associations require direct exposure-based experimental validation.

title: Context-dependent localization and expression of glutamate and GABA and their machinery in microglia.
abstract: Microglia are central regulators of brain homeostasis and synaptic architecture, but whether they, like astrocytes, act as reservoirs and handlers of glutamate and GABA is unknown. Using post-embedding immunogold electron microscopy, we provide the first ultrastructural evidence that individual microglial processes contain GABA and glutamate. At the nanoscale, glutamate-positive microglial processes were preferentially apposed to glutamatergic terminals, whereas GABA-positive processes showed no consistent spatial relationship to GABAergic boutons. At the microscale, spatial transcriptomics revealed that microglial somata expressing GABA-handling genes are enriched in GABAergic neuron-rich regions, while microglia expressing glutamate-handling genes are enriched in glutamatergic neuron-rich regions. Analysis of four single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets (6,594,428 cells, including 320,683 microglia) demonstrated conserved expression of glutamate and GABA transport and metabolism genes in microglia across species, corroborated at the protein level by proteomics and in situ by confocal microscopy. Functionally, acute neuroinflammation selectively depleted microglial GABA content by 57% while leaving glutamate unchanged, indicating differential vulnerability of these amino acid pools. Together, these multimodal data identify microglia as previously unrecognized reservoirs of the brain's principal inhibitory and excitatory transmitters, with spatially adapted handling machinery, and implicate them as potential contributors to excitation-inhibition homeostasis within the quad-partite synapse.

title: The HOXC6-orchestrated COL10A1/ITGB1 axis induces epithelial-mesenchymal transition to drive gastric cancer progression.
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is characterized by high aggressiveness and heterogeneity, leading to poor prognosis and treatment resistance. Here, we aimed to screen reliable biomarkers of GC to assist clinicians improve the survival rate of GC patients. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified from three datasets: TCGA-STAD, GSE54129, and GSE13911, and were cross-analyzed. The overlapping upregulated DEGs were validated in the RNA sequencing dataset of GC clinical samples, and the key regulatory gene HOXC6 was screened. GO and KEGG analyses revealed prominent enrichment in extracellular matrix organization and the ECM-receptor interaction pathway. Moreover, HOXC6 was significantly overexpressed in GC tissues, and GC patients with high HOXC6 expression had a shorter overall survival. Overexpression of HOXC6 significantly promoted GC cell proliferation, invasion and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), while HOXC6 knockdown had the opposite effect. The mechanism study revealed that HOXC6 transcriptionally activated COL10A1, which interacted with ITGB1 protein to promote the activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. Activated β-catenin translocated into the nucleus to promote the transcriptional activation of MMP9, thus promoting the EMT in GC cells. Knockdown of COL10A1, ITGB1 or MMP9 inhibited the EMT and malignant growth of GC cells. Finally, a xenograft tumor model was constructed in vivo, and it was found that HOXC6 knockdown inhibited tumor growth and blocked the activation of the COL10A1/ITGB1/Wnt/β-catenin/MMP9 signaling axis. Overall, HOXC6 drives the malignant progression of GC through the COL10A1/ITGB1/Wnt/β-catenin/MMP9 signaling axis, suggesting that HOXC6 may be a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target for GC.

title: Conserved Transcriptomic Heat Stress Response Signatures in Coral Recruits From Crosses of Thermally Distinct Broodstock.
abstract: Thermal history provenancing can guide the choice of parental broodstock for selective breeding of corals from distinct reefs and has been proposed as an intervention for enhancing climate resilience. However, the genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying resultant offspring responses to heat stress, particularly during early life stages, remain poorly understood. Here, we generated Acropora tersa larvae and recruits by crossing parental colonies from the historically warmer Martin Reef and cooler Davies Reef and assessed the effects of within- and between-reef crosses on genetic diversity using single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) genotyping and transcriptional responses to heat stress using ribonucleic acid sequencing (RNA-seq). Genome-wide SNP analyses showed that broodstock from Martin and Davies Reefs were weakly differentiated (FST = 0.008) and exhibited comparable heterozygosity, as did all larval offspring groups. Host RNA-seq analyses of surviving recruits exposed to heat stress (32°C for 36 days) revealed that the within- and between-reef offspring groups (n = 2 and 1 respectively) activated conserved stress-response pathways, with seven genotype-independent heat-responsive genes detected across all offspring groups. Differential expression and enrichment analyses showed induction of defence, protein homeostasis, intracellular transport, and metabolic processes alongside repression of growth- and signaling-related functions, consistent with the Type A General Coral Stress Response. Taken together, these findings indicate that within- and between-reef offspring generated to test thermal history provenancing exhibited broadly similar genetic diversity and weak differentiation alongside largely conserved host transcriptional responses to heat stress, including seven genotype-independent heat-responsive candidate genes.

title: Artemetin Confers Neuroprotection in Spinal Cord Injury by Targeting Ferroptosis.
abstract: Ferroptosis plays a critical role in secondary neuronal death following spinal cord injury (SCI). Active ingredients from traditional Chinese medicine exhibit significant potential in neuroprotection. Artemetin, a potential neuroprotective agent, has an unclear effect and mechanism on ferroptosis after SCI. The study employed in vitro and in vivo models. The effects of artemetin were evaluated employing assays for cell viability and ferroptosis-associated indices (e.g., Fe2+, GPX4, lipid peroxidation), sequencing analyses (scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-Seq), and interaction validation (molecular docking, MST). This study found through in vivo and in vitro experiments that artemetin significantly improves motor function in SCI rats, alleviates iron overload and lipid peroxidation in spinal cord tissue, and increases neuronal survival. In VSC4.1 cells, artemetin effectively antagonizes erastin-induced ferroptosis. Mechanistically, transcriptomics, molecular docking, and microcalorimetry experiments indicate that artemetin binds to and downregulates the ferroptosis-promoting protein ACSL4. Overexpression of ACSL4 can reverse the protective effects of artemetin. In summary, this study demonstrates that artemetin inhibits neuronal ferroptosis by targeting ACSL4, providing a new potential strategy for SCI treatment.

title: Lactylation-regulated METTL3-mediated cholesterol metabolic reprogramming via FDFT1 facilitates macrophage polarization in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits limited clinical response to immunotherapy, highlighting the pressing need for novel strategies targeting its immunosuppressive microenvironment. While metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic alterations contribute to malignancy, the role of lactate-driven protein lactylation in remodeling the tumor microenvironment remains elusive. This study aimed to investigate the role of histone and non-histone lactylation in HCC, focusing on its regulatory impact on cholesterol metabolism and anti-tumor immune responses. To elucidate novel epigenetic mechanisms driven by lactate-induced histone and non-histone lactylation, global lactylome profiling was implemented in this study. Additionally, customized site-specific antibodies, RNA sequencing, lipidomics, and single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) validation were employed to systematically investigate the underlying regulatory network. Next, spontaneous orthotopic HCC mouse models, humanized orthotopic HCC models, and flow cytometry were utilized to explore the functional characteristics of METTL3-K27 lactylation. Mechanistically, H3K18 lactylation upregulated METTL3 expression, while site-specific METTL3 K27 lactylation facilitated m⁶A modification of FDFT1 transcripts. Moreover, IGF2BP2 recognized these epitranscriptomic marks to promote FDFT1 translation, thereby enhancing cholesterol biosynthesis and efflux. Then, this metabolite-driven reprogramming polarized tumor-associated macrophages toward an immunosuppressive M2 phenotype. These findings highlighted the pivotal role of the H3K18la/METTL3-K27la/FDFT1 axis in reprogramming the TME. Consequently, targeting this pathway may alleviate immunosuppression in HCC, establishing a novel therapeutic strategy that interconnects histone lactylation, non-histone lactylation, cholesterol metabolic reprogramming, and immune modulation.

title: Celastrol partially restores Prodh expression in oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-injured astrocytes: A candidate mechanism relevant to ischemic stroke.
abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is an acute cerebrovascular disease caused by obstruction of the cerebral arteries, which deprives brain tissue of oxygen and glucose. This deprivation perturbs endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis and activates the unfolded protein response (UPR). When ER stress (ERS) is severe or sustained, the UPR can no longer restore homeostasis and cell injury ensues. Celastrol, a pentacyclic triterpene compound derived from Tripterygium wilfordii, a medicinal plant used in traditional Chinese medicine, alleviates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by regulating astrocyte function. However, whether celastrol can treat IS by relieving ERS remains unclear. Bulk transcriptomic (GSE202659) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; GSE233812) datasets were downloaded from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Differential expression analysis, functional enrichment analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, random-forest, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction, and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were used to identify candidate gene of celastrol in IS. scRNA-seq analysis was then applied to examine the cell-type distribution of these genes and the biological functions of the astrocytes in which they act. Integrated analysis suggested that Prodh is a candidate ERS-related gene predominantly expressed in astrocytes. In cultured astrocytes subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R), Prodh mRNA was downregulated, and celastrol treatment partially restored its expression; this restoration was accompanied by improved cell viability in the CCK-8 assay. In addition, scRNA-seq analysis revealed that Prodh expression decreased at days 1 and 3 after IS and increased by day 7. These findings identify Prodh as a candidate gene in astrocytes after ischemic stroke. Celastrol partially restored Prodh expression in OGD/R-injured astrocytes, and this restoration was accompanied by improved cell viability , which supports further investigation into the functional significance of this restoration.

title: The KL and TLE1 anoikis-related signature predicts the diagnosis and indicates immune characteristics in endometriosis.
abstract: Endometriosis (EMs) lacks non-invasive diagnostic biomarkers. Anoikis resistance enables ectopic endometrial cell survival, but key anoikis-related genes (ARGs) remain unclear. We aimed to identify a robust ARG-based diagnostic signature for EMs and explore its immune associations. Four transcriptomic datasets (GSE7307 training; GSE7305, GSE23339, GSE51981 validation) were analyzed. DE-ARGs were identified by overlapping DEGs with 434 ARGs from GeneCards. Three machine learning algorithms (LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE) screened core genes. ROC analysis evaluated diagnostic performance. A two-gene logistic regression model combining KL and TLE1 was also constructed, and its ROC performance was evaluated across training and validation cohorts. CIBERSORT and ssGSEA assessed immune infiltration. Single-cell RNA-seq (GSE179640) defined cell-type expression. qPCR and Western blotting validated expression in a small independent clinical cohort (n = 3 per group). 196 DE-ARGs were identified, significantly enriched in PI3K-AKT and focal adhesion pathways. KL and TLE1 were selected as core genes by all three algorithms. Both were consistently downregulated in EMs tissues across all cohorts (training AUC: KL=0.952, TLE1 =0.973; validation sets up to 1.000), substantially outperforming CA-125. The combined KL/TLE1 logistic model achieved AUCs of 1.000 in GSE7307, 1.000 in GSE7305, 1.000 in GSE23339, and 0.817 in GSE51981. Immune profiling revealed an immunosuppressive microenvironment with increased M2 macrophages and decreased NK cells, which correlated with KL/TLE1 downregulation. These findings indicate an association rather than a proven causal relationship. Single-cell analysis localized TLE1 to epithelial cells and KL to endothelial and fibroblast subsets. qPCR and Western blotting confirmed significant downregulation at both mRNA and protein levels. The KL/TLE1 signature exhibits excellent diagnostic accuracy for endometriosis in tissue-based analyses. This signature holds promise as a tissue-based diagnostic tool, but clinical translation will require larger prospective cohorts and validation in non-invasive samples such as menstrual effluent or circulating exosomes.
